title: Climate-Adaptive AI for Multimodal Biodiversity Monitoring: Integrating Passive Acoustics, Camera Traps, and Species Distribution Modeling under Environmental Nonstationarity
background:
Biodiversity loss accelerated by anthropogenic climate change demands continental-scale monitoring infrastructure capable of detecting species occurrence, abundance, and range shifts at ecologically relevant timescales. Recent advances in passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) and camera trap networks have generated petabyte-scale ecological datasets, with foundation models such as BirdNET-Analyzer v2 [1] and MegaDetector-Eco [2] achieving strong in-distribution performance for species classification. Concurrently, deep species distribution models (SDMs) leveraging remote sensing covariates have improved range projections under shared socioeconomic pathway scenarios [3], while contrastive multimodal pretraining on geo-tagged audio-visual ecological data has shown promise for label-efficient transfer [4].

Despite these advances, critical gaps remain. First, current models exhibit severe performance degradation under distribution shift induced by novel acoustic backgrounds, climate-driven phenological mismatches, and emerging species assemblages absent from training corpora [5]. Second, integration across modalities is largely post-hoc: acoustic detections, image-based occurrences, and abiotic covariates are rarely fused within a single probabilistic framework that propagates detection uncertainty into downstream SDM inference [6]. Third, long-tailed taxonomic distributions, citizen-science label noise, and severe geographic sampling bias in the Global South undermine equitable monitoring. Finally, existing SDMs assume stationarity in species-environment relationships, an assumption violated under rapid climate change, leading to systematically biased range forecasts. Addressing these gaps requires AI methods that are jointly robust, multimodal, uncertainty-aware, and explicitly nonstationary.
challenges: Developing domain-generalizable acoustic and visual recognition models that maintain calibrated performance under climate-driven shifts in soundscape composition, vegetation phenology, and diel activity patterns not represented in training data

Designing a unified probabilistic multimodal framework that fuses PAM detections, camera trap imagery, and remote sensing covariates while propagating per-detection confidence into hierarchical occupancy and abundance estimators

Mitigating long-tailed class imbalance and geographic sampling bias for rare and cryptic taxa, including techniques for few-shot adaptation, label-noise-robust training on citizen-science data, and active sensor placement under budget constraints

Constructing nonstationary species distribution models that explicitly represent time-varying species-environment relationships, no-analog future climates, and biotic interaction shifts, with quantified epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty for conservation decision-making

Achieving on-device, energy-constrained inference for solar-powered edge deployments in remote ecosystems, including model compression, event-triggered sensing, and federated continual learning across heterogeneous sensor networks
